model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, preference-share dividends, perpetual-bond coupons and NCI charged in the flow

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 357,113 (interim line 447, +8.41% YoY; NII +10.2% on NIM 1.27% +1bp and asset growth) + H2 2026E 345,300 (H2 2025 actual 330,448 = FY2025 659,866 - H1 2025 329,418, x 1.045; the H1 growth rate is flattered by a weak H1 2025 NII base and is not extrapolated). FY2025 actual 659,866 (annual line 573, +4.28%). Operating income = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other non-interest income, the Bank's own top line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 322,212,411,814 ordinary shares = 238,590,135,419 A shares + 83,622,276,395 H shares (FY2025 annual line 6389; interim line 4158), one class with identical economic rights. Basic = diluted (no potentially dilutive instruments, annual line 12083); weighted average FY2025 309,482m because the MOF placement of 27,824m A shares at RMB5.93 (RMB165.0bn) settled in June 2025. Held FLAT: no share scheme, no convertible; preference shares and perpetual bonds are non-convertible AT1 (write-down trigger, not conversion). The dilution the flat count ignores is another state placement at a discount to book, which the bear scenario treats through its higher capital target rather than a share count.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits RMB26.8tn at 30 Jun 2026, due to central banks, interbank funding, debt securities issued (incl. TLAC non-capital bonds) are operating funding and cash/central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route and nothing is bridged after the flows. The CSV total_debt (RMB2.26tn debt securities issued) is NOT used.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE: profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~241,300 (PBT 702,400 x 45.5% = 319,600 less income tax ~15.5%, NCI ~5.0% and preference/perpetual distributions ~4.0% of PBT = 24.5%) LESS the equity retained to hold CET1 at 12.0% on FY2026E RWA RMB23.0tn versus FY2025 net CET1 2,622,071 (0.12 x 23,000,000 - 2,622,071 = 137,929). FY2025 actual: profit to equity holders 243,021 less AT1 distributions 13,834 = 229,187 to ordinary shareholders (annual line 12088). Reported OCF (FY2025 812,030; FY2024 550,966; FY2022 -21,855) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used; the CSV's NULL free_cash_flow is correct.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme, share option or employee share plan in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports or the H1 2026 interim; basic = diluted EPS (RMB0.74 FY2025); no share repurchases in any year. House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate (null).
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1751 at 2026-10-23T09:20Z, Yahoo Finance. Consistent with the 1.1738 used for 3618.HK on 2026-10-22. The Shanghai A share (601988.SS) trades at a persistent A/H premium normal for Chinese banks, so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H shares; H-share dividends are declared in RMB and paid in HKD or RMB by election.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.cet1_anchor: CET1 ratio 12.04% on RWA RMB22,276,506m at 30 Jun 2026 (interim lines 477-483; net CET1 2,681,031); 12.53% on 20,932,851 at FY2025 (annual lines 5769-5773; net CET1 2,622,071); 12.20% on 19,217,559 at FY2024. RWA grew 8.9% in FY2025 and 6.4% in H1 2026 alone; net CET1 rose 11.9% in FY2025 only because of the RMB165bn MOF placement, and the ratio fell 49bp in H1 2026 as the injection is deployed. FY2026E: RWA ~23.0tn (+10%), net CET1 ~2,768,700 (H1 2,681,031 + H2 ordinary profit ~126,000 - 2026 interim dividend 38,343 declared at RMB0.119/share) = ~12.0%. Tier 1 13.65%, total CAR 18.31%. Regulatory minimum as a G-SIB/D-SIB: CET1 9.00%, Tier 1 10.00%, total 12.00% (annual lines 18330-18332). TLAC (16% of RWA from 2025, 18% from 2028) is met with TLAC non-capital bonds, a funding cost inside NII, not an equity call.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 9.5% in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights and the bear's capital target, not by moving the discount rate). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION: not fetched; the PBOC easing cycle has kept the 10Y CGB in the 1.6-2.0% range since 2025) + beta ~1.0 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.3%, plus ~1.2pt for risks a CSI-300 ERP does not price for an H-share holder in a state bank: state-directed lending under the 'five major tasks', property/LGFV exposure, dilutive policy placements (June 2025 at RMB5.93 vs BVPS 8.18, ~9.5% dilution), sanctions/compliance exposure on the largest cross-border book of the Big Four, and capital-account/RMB risk. Set EQUAL to the 9.5% used for CCB/0939.HK and PSBC/1658.HK (Big Four/Six, MOF-recapitalised) and one point below the 10.5% used for CITIC/0998.HK and CQRCB/3618.HK: BOC is a G-SIB with a 3pt CET1 buffer over its 9.0% minimum, NPL 1.22%, coverage 200%, the lowest funding cost in the system and 28% of pre-tax profit earned outside the mainland (BOCHK). Not a USD or HKD rate. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities RMB18,375m (FY2025 annual line 14386) are immaterial against RMB3.1tn equity and are operating funding inside operating expenses; nothing is bridged.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI (RMB144,080m, mainly BOCHK minorities; FY2025 share of profit 14,915 = 4.95% of PBT) is charged inside cash_tax_rate_path together with income tax and AT1 distributions, so the flow is attributable to ORDINARY shareholders of the Bank; nothing is deducted in the bridge. Charged once.
inputs.at1_treatment: Preference-share dividends and perpetual (undated capital) bond coupons - RMB13,834m declared in FY2025, 8,269m in H1 2026 (interim line 6192) - are charged inside cash_tax_rate_path (~4.0% of PBT in FY2026E after the RMB140bn of perpetual redemptions and RMB100bn of issuance over 2025-H1 2026). These instruments rank ahead of ordinary shareholders and are NOT equity for this valuation; the RMB3.1tn shareholders' equity in the CSV includes ~RMB250bn of them.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalised at the cost of equity via the engine route, consistent with 2016.HK, 0998.HK, 3618.HK and 1658.HK. Routing: SKILL.md 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift' row. The engine's component fields are re-purposed: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin_path = profit-before-tax margin (after operating expenses and credit impairment); da_pct_path = 0 (D&A is inside operating expenses, not added back); cash_tax_rate_path = income tax + NCI + preference/perpetual distributions as a share of PBT, so NOPAT is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders; capex_pct_path = equity retained to hold the CET1 target on growing RWA (the bank's reinvestment); wc_capture_pct = 0; net_debt = 0; terminal_cap_multiple is a P/E-style cap on FCFE that does not bind. Owner-FCF mechanics (SBC, interest income, lease, EV bridge) do not apply: deposits are not debt, OCF is meaningless for a bank. Valued in CNY and converted at fx_rate; unsuffixed per-share values are HKD. No SBC in any year, so house = street and band_position is null.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Operating income path: 3-year revenue CAGR 4.0% (FY2022 586,461 -> FY2025 659,866), tempered by NIM compression (1.75% -> 1.26%) that has held net-income growth to 2.4%; base case fades 4% to 3%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity CAGR 8.1-8.5% exceeds revenue (3-4%) and EPS (1-4%) by more than 30%: equity growth includes the RMB165bn MOF A-share placement (June 2025), net AT1 issuance and retained earnings at a 30% payout, so it is not an earnings-growth signal. BVPS grew 6.2% (3yr) and fell to 8.36 at FY2025 from a pre-placement run-rate above 8.5 because the placement price (5.93) was below book (8.18).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for a bank (reported OCF swings between -484bn and +843bn on deposit flows); FCFE on the CET1-retention basis is the flow valued. EPS FY2025 0.74 vs FY2024 0.75 reflects the 9.5% share-count dilution, not a profit decline (profit to ordinary shareholders +3.5%).

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +4% in FY2027-28 fading to 3%: NIM has bottomed around 1.25-1.30% (H1 2026 1.27%, +1bp after -69bp over seven years) but further LPR cuts cap any recovery; interest-earning assets +7% slowing to +4%; fee income low single digit (FY2025 +7.4% off a weak FY2024); other non-interest income not extrapolated. Below the 6.5% FY2026E and well below the H1 2026 +8.4%.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after operating expenses and credit impairment. FY2022 48.4%, FY2023 47.4%, FY2024 46.6%, FY2025 45.7%, H1 2026 ~45.5% (impairment +18% YoY). Base eases to 44%: credit cost normalises from the FY2025 low of 0.48% towards ~0.6% as property/LGFV workouts continue, cost-to-income holds ~28%, no NIM recovery. The 200% allowance coverage is a cushion the model does not release.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 on a target gliding 12.0% (FY2026E) -> 11.9, 11.8, 11.7, 11.6, 11.5% (FY2031 onward) on RWA growth of 7.0, 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.5% from FY2026E RWA RMB23.0tn and net CET1 ~2,768.7bn. The 0.5pt glide is the stated purpose of the 2025 MOF injection (deploy capital into credit growth) and lands at the 11.3-11.8% the Bank ran at in FY2019-FY2023, still 2.5pt above its 9.0% G-SIB minimum. FY2027 retention 159.9bn = 0.119 x 24,610bn - 2,768.7bn (21.9% of income); FY2031 139.2bn; converging on 0.035 x 0.115 x prior RWA = 144bn in FY2036 (14.8% of income). Terminal-year CET1 ~RMB4.26tn on RWA 37.1tn; terminal ROE on CET1 ~7.6%.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~15.5% of PBT (FY2025 14.4%, FY2024 14.3%, H1 2026 ~19% - low because of tax-exempt government-bond interest, with H1 seasonally higher) + NCI ~5.0% (FY2025 4.95%; BOCHK minorities) + preference-share dividends and perpetual-bond coupons ~4.0% (FY2025 13,834 = 4.6%; ~12.5bn in FY2026E after net AT1 redemption) = 24.5%. FY2025 actual total 23.9%. AT1 coupons are fixed in RMB so their share falls as PBT grows; ignored (conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 9.5% - 3.0% = 15.4x; the 18x cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B on CET1 ~0.65x at terminal ROE on CET1 ~7.6%, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = 0.71.
base.narrative: Steady-state G-SIB: NIM holds ~1.25-1.30%, credit cost normalises modestly, RWA growth decelerates from 7% to 3.5% and CET1 glides to 11.5% as the MOF injection is deployed. FCFE ~RMB88bn in FY2027 against an ordinary dividend of ~RMB74bn (30% payout), rising to ~RMB179bn by FY2036 as retention falls.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovers to ~1.4% as deposit repricing catches up with asset yields and the PBOC pauses; overseas (BOCHK, RMB clearing, Belt and Road) keeps growing operating income +11% as in FY2025; wealth and pension fees compound. Still below the FY2025-26 overseas pace.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost stays ~0.5% as property NPL formation keeps falling (NPL 1.22% and improving), cost-to-income holds the H1 2026 improvement; margin returns to the FY2023 47.4% level.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 target glides 12.0% -> 11.25% by FY2031 (2.25pt over the 9.0% minimum, the Bank's FY2019-21 level) on RWA growth of 7.0, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.5, 3.5, 3.5% - advanced-approach RWA optimisation lets assets grow faster than RWA. FY2027 retention 147.6bn (19.8% of income) falling to 12.9% from FY2032.
bull.tax_rationale: As base, with the fixed-RMB AT1 coupon share shrinking faster on higher PBT.
bull.narrative: NIM recovery plus overseas growth lift operating income 6% fading to 3.5%, margin back to 47.5%, capital deployed down to 11.25% CET1. FCFE ~RMB115bn in FY2027, ~RMB245bn by FY2036.

bear.growth_rationale: Another leg of PBOC easing takes NIM to ~1.10%; loan growth is policy-directed into low-yield 'five major tasks' lending; operating income flat for two years then +2%, below RWA growth throughout so NI/RWA keeps falling.
bear.margin_rationale: Property and LGFV losses crystallise: credit cost rises to ~0.8% (FY2018 level), coverage is drawn down rather than rebuilt, cost-to-income drifts up on compliance spend (sanctions screening on the cross-border book). Margin falls to 41%, below any year in the FY2017-FY2025 history.
bear.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 12.0% throughout (no release of the MOF buffer: the regulator keeps the G-SIB/TLAC buffer requirements rising and the state wants headroom for countercyclical lending) on RWA growth of 8.0, 7.0, 6.0, 5.0, 4.0, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0, 3.0% - policy lending grows the balance sheet faster than the revenue it earns. FY2027 retention 212.1bn = 29.9% of income; the ordinary dividend (~RMB70bn) exceeds FCFE (~RMB17bn) in FY2027-28 and is funded by another discounted state placement, which is the dilution this scenario expresses through retention rather than a share count.
bear.tax_rationale: As base plus 0.5pt: AT1 coupons are fixed while PBT stagnates, and the tax-exempt bond share shrinks.
bear.narrative: Japanification: NIM 1.1%, credit cost 0.8%, flat revenue, RWA still growing 8% on policy lending with CET1 pinned at 12%. FCFE ~RMB17bn in FY2027, below the dividend, recovering to ~RMB130bn by FY2036 only because RWA growth converges on 3%.

scenario_narratives.base: Steady-state G-SIB. Operating income +4% fading to +3% on a NIM that has bottomed at ~1.27%, pre-tax margin eases to 44% as credit cost normalises from 0.48%, RWA growth slows from 7% to 3.5% and the CET1 ratio glides from 12.0% to 11.5% as the June 2025 MOF injection is deployed. FCFE covers the ~30% ordinary payout from FY2027. Terminal P/B on CET1 ~0.65x at a 7.6% ROE on CET1.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM recovers toward 1.4% as deposit repricing catches up, overseas (BOCHK, RMB clearing, Belt and Road) keeps growing double digit, credit cost stays ~0.5% with NPL still improving; margin back to 47.5% and capital run down to 11.25% CET1. Operating income +6% fading to +3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Another easing leg takes NIM to ~1.1%, property/LGFV losses crystallise (credit cost 0.8%, margin 41%), policy lending grows RWA 8% while revenue stalls, and CET1 is held at 12% so the dividend exceeds FCFE for two years and is funded by another discounted state placement.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the house default 15%, below the 30-35% used for the joint-stock and regional precedents 0998.HK/3618.HK/1658.HK): BOC's capital (CET1 12.04%, 3pt above its 9.0% G-SIB minimum, freshly recapitalised by the MOF), asset quality (NPL 1.22% and improving, coverage 200%) and 28% of pre-tax profit earned outside the mainland argue for less downside weight than a single-market Chinese bank, but NIM is the thinnest in the group at 1.27%, property/LGFV exposure is sector-wide, the state has shown it will dilute at a discount to book, and the cross-border book carries sanctions risk no peer has. Bull 25% (above the 20% the precedents use): H1 2026 showed NIM +1bp, operating income +8.4% and cost-to-income 23.4%, and the overseas franchise is a genuine growth engine the mainland-only banks lack. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Chinese state bank is a regulated capital-allocation vehicle: value is the stream of profit to ordinary shareholders after tax, minorities and AT1 coupons, less the equity the regulator and the state require it to retain to carry a growing risk-weighted balance sheet, discounted at a CNY cost of equity. Deposits and bonds are funding, not debt; reported OCF is meaningless; the share count is flat because SBC is zero, but the state's willingness to place shares below book (June 2025) is the dilution to watch. The CET1 target and RWA growth are the levers that matter more than NIM: a 0.5pt change in the long-run CET1 target is worth ~RMB115bn of equity, about RMB0.36/share.
key_risks_to_valuation: CET1 target: if the state keeps the ratio at 12%+ (bear) rather than letting it glide to 11.5% (base), ~RMB115bn of FCFE never reaches shareholders
RWA growth above revenue growth: policy-directed lending into low-yield sectors grows the capital requirement faster than earnings
NIM: every 10bp on ~RMB35tn of interest-earning assets is ~RMB35bn of operating income (5%), ~RMB27bn of ordinary profit
Credit cost: property and LGFV losses crystallising takes credit cost from 0.48% toward 0.8% (bear), ~RMB75bn of impairment on a RMB24.7tn loan book
Dilutive state placements at a discount to book (June 2025: RMB5.93 vs BVPS 8.18) if the dividend keeps exceeding FCFE
Sanctions/compliance on the largest cross-border and correspondent book of the Big Four (Russia-linked transactions)
CNY/HKD: the valuation is in CNY; a 5% RMB depreciation against HKD is ~5% off the HKD value with no change in the business
Cost of equity: 9.5% assumes a ~1.8% CGB yield and a 6.5% ERP; at 10.5% (the joint-stock precedent rate) the base value falls ~15%

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 4.30-6.29 HKD
data_sources.fx: Yahoo Finance CNYHKD=X at inputs.fx_note timestamp
data_sources.financials: 3988.HK_Metrics.csv and kpis (core_metrics) from the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports and the H1 2024-H1 2026 interim reports; RWA, net CET1, AT1 distributions and profit to ordinary shareholders read directly from 3988.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (lines 573-605, 1950-1957, 5769-5773, 12083-12094, 18330-18332) and 3988.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (lines 447-483, 1186-1192, 4892-4894, 6186-6200)
data_sources.qualitative: 3988.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-23): business model, overseas mix, MOF recapitalisation, risks, guidance
